A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for the class of codes we consider, nonlinear receivers can provide only a marginal performance advantage over linear ones, whereas the latter are much simpler to implement and can provide an important gain in terms of complexity.
, for the considered codes, the nonlinear iterative receiver offers the best performance, while the simple linear receiver is the worst.
, for the codes considered, the iterative receiver offers the same performance as the nonlinear receiver, with the advantage of being simpler and faster.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the design and analysis of suboptimum receivers for space-time codes should be based on the notion of a "good" code, i.e., a code with good error performance when used in conjunction with a suitable receiver, rather than on the notion of an "optimum" code.

, when the receiver is linear, the performance of the space-time code is not improved much by using a more complex receiver interface, and, in fact, the nonlinear interface is not even better than a linear interface based on the Viterbi algorithm.
, in this setting, the use of a suboptimum receiver interface may be more beneficial than the use of a more sophisticated space-time code.
